title: Cobalt on-prem field notebook
content:
Day 1 quick log - CobaltHealth (on-prem VPC)

Context / goals:
- Sit with on-site infra lead (James) to finish private deployment MVP for CobaltHealth. Goal: get one small production-like inference cluster up behind their VPC NAT and validate end-to-end inference against their sample workload (speech-to-text postprocessing + small reranking flow).
- Validate: model loads, KV cache behavior for 2 concurrent demo clients, basic tracing to our console, and backup/restore of model artifacts to customer S3-compatible storage.

Notes from kickoff (09:10)
- On-site network: split-routing via firewall (Palo Alto). Outbound to 52.18.0.0/16 allowed for Redwood egress only.
- Customer S3 endpoint: https://s3.cobalt.internal (self-signed cert). They want us to use customer-managed KMS.
- MTU on the VM network is 1400 (important — had packet fragmentation when trying 1500).
- Proxy: corporate outbound proxy at 10.12.0.6:3128 — we must set NO_PROXY for internal 10.0.0.0/8 ranges.

Immediate checklist (run today)
- [x] Confirm host inventory and rack power (done by field ops at 09:25)
- [x] Bootstrap base VM image (ubuntu-22.04) with docker (09:45)
- [x] Pull redwood-private-runtime:stable-2026-02 (09:58)
- [ ] Confirm KMS integration (blocked)
- [x] Configure local DNS overrides (hosts) for internal S3 (10:20)
- [ ] Smoke test model load (blocked by KMS)
- [ ] Run two-client throughput test (after model loads)
- [ ] Wire up tracing to console (token exchange pending)

Commands run (notes)
- docker pull ghcr.io/redwood-inference/private-runtime:stable-2026-02
- sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1   # enabled for host routing
- export NO_PROXY=10.0.0.0/8,127.0.0.1
- ./deploy/local-k8s-up --image redwood/private-runtime:stable-2026-02 --nodes 3 --mtu 1400
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide

Blockers / open questions
- KMS: Customer's KMS team has a policy requiring 2-step approval for any external key usage. They have not yet created the service-principal binding. Ticket OPS-783 is open. Without KMS we cannot mount encrypted model artifacts (we can test unencrypted fallback with explicit approval).
- Proxy auth: proxy requires NTLM auth in their environment. Our runtime lacks an NTLM agent; Diego thinks we can tunnel via a small squid sidecar. Need approval from James.
- TLS: their internal CA is self-signed. Console token exchange fails TLS verification. Quick workaround: add CA to runtime CA bundle on nodes (done as temporary flag --insecure-ca-path /etc/ssl/cobalt-ca.pem), but this must be recorded in handoff.

Workarounds attempted
- Started runtime with MODEL_STORE_READ_UNENCRYPTED=1 to validate model load path — success for local debug models but not allowed for production.
- Deployed a squid proxy sidecar on control plane to handle NTLM handshake. Preliminary success, but perf impact unknown.

Measurements observed
- Model cold load (small L2 reranker ~300M params) cold-start ~18s on a single A10G-equivalent node with quantized weights.
- KV cache warmup dramatically reduces token generation latency after first 20 requests (p50 from 120ms -> 38ms in our quick test).

Handoff notes for on-site tech (James)
- If you reboot nodes, ensure etcd pods come up before runtime pods (kube-system readiness). Use: kubectl wait --for=condition=available deployment/etcd -n kube-system --timeout=300s
- If S3 access fails: check that the S3 endpoint DNS resolves to 10.45.x.x range and that the host CA /etc/ssl/cobalt-ca.pem is present and referenced by /etc/containers/registries.conf (containerd).
- Proxy: if you see 407s in runtime logs, firewall likely splitting NTLM session. Restart squid sidecar after ensuring proxy credentials env set in /etc/redwood/proxy.env

TODO (next actions)
- [ ] Ops ticket update: push KMS approval request and include exact principal: svc:redwood-deploy@cobalt
- [ ] Prep short doc for security team describing risk if we enable MODEL_STORE_READ_UNENCRYPTED
- [ ] Bench script: add a small load runner that simulates 2x concurrent chat + 1x batch embeddings stream
- [ ] Run end-to-end tracing once token exchange fixed (need console token from Diego)
- [ ] Add automated reboot test to ensure PV reattachment for model cache

Random reminders / context bits
- Customer asked: "can Redwood run without internet access?" Short answer: yes, but requires pre-staged model artifacts and we need the console proxy token exchange to be done offline (manual token file exchange). Note this in handoff.
- Keep an eye on disk IO on model-store nodes — their NVMe is shared with local backup jobs that run at 02:00 by default.

Session log snippets
- 09:58: pulled image
- 10:20: set hosts override for s3.cobalt.internal -> 10.45.2.3
- 11:05: runtime pods in CrashLoopBackOff -> found proxy 407s
- 11:42: spun up squid sidecar, transient success

Lessons learned
- Bring a CA bundle and simple proxy sidecar for NTLM-enabled clients.
- MTU mismatch will silently wreck large batch transfers — test with 1x and 4x batch sizes early.
- Always verify KMS bindings before attempting encrypted artifact flows.

Attachments / followups
- Attach cert: /tmp/cobalt-ca.pem (hand this to security)
- Follow-up with Diego on console token exchange (he will create one-time token today)

End of Day 1 notes — Avery
